extDesc.message: Clear browsing data in one click.

keepWhatsApp.message: Stay signed in to WhatsApp Web

keepWhatsAppNote.message: Leaves cookies and site data for web.whatsapp.com alone when cleaning, so you do not have to link your phone again. The cache is still cleared.

keepTelegram.message: Stay signed in to Telegram Web

keepTelegramNote.message: Leaves cookies and site data for web.telegram.org alone when cleaning, so you do not have to sign in again. The cache is still cleared.

keepSitesNoteFirefox.message: Not available in Firefox, which cannot leave one site out when clearing local storage and IndexedDB. To stay signed in, leave Local storage, IndexedDB and Service workers unticked.

autoClean.message: Clean automatically when the browser closes

autoCleanNote.message: Uses the items selected in the popup and always covers all time. Sweep tries when the last window closes and cleans again at the next startup, because a browser may quit before an extension finishes.

whitelistHintChromium.message: One domain per line. Cookies are kept for the whole domain, including subdomains. Other site data (local storage, IndexedDB, service workers) is kept only for the exact host you list, so add app.example.com as well if that is where you sign in.

whitelistHintFirefox.message: One domain per line. Cookies are kept for each listed domain and its subdomains. Other site data is still cleared. Firefox will ask for permission to read cookies on all sites; Sweep uses it only to find which hosts to clear.

errCookiePermission.message: Cookies were not cleared: the whitelist needs the cookie permission. Open Settings and save again to grant it.

updateNoteChrome.message: When you open Sweep, at most once every 6 hours, it reads Google’s public list of Chrome releases and shows a red badge if yours is older. This is the only time Sweep uses the network, and it sends nothing about you.

updateNoteBrave.message: When you open Sweep, at most once every 6 hours, it reads Brave’s latest release from GitHub and shows a red badge if yours is older. Brave hides its exact version from extensions, so only major updates are noticed. This is the only time Sweep uses the network, and it sends nothing about you.

updateNoteFirefox.message: When you open Sweep, at most once every 6 hours, it reads Mozilla’s public list of Firefox releases and shows a red badge if yours is older. This is the only time Sweep uses the network, and it sends nothing about you.

updateHowFirefox.message: Open Menu > Help > About Firefox to update.

keepLook.message: See what is here and choose what to keep

keepNoteHistory.message: Switch a site on and its pages stay in your history when you clean. The number is how many pages it has there.

keepNoteDownloads.message: Switch a site on and its download records are kept when you clean. The number is how many downloads came from it. Sweep never deletes the downloaded files themselves.

keepNoteCookies.message: Switch a site on and its cookies, and those of its subdomains, are kept when you clean. The browser does not let extensions list cookies, so these are the sites you visited.

keepNoteSites.message: Switch a site on and this data is kept for it when you clean. The browser does not let extensions list it, so these are the sites you visited. Use the exact site name, such as app.example.com.

keepSearch.message: Search, or type a site to add
